column2: How do I link a memory to a piece of furniture or a room?
column3: Click the piece of furniture or the room, then “🔗 Link a memory”: a photo or a document, a story, a person, or a family memory. A ✦ appears on the plan and in 3D; a click on it (even during the visit) shows the memory. House tab → “🏷 The memories of the house” to see them all.

column2: How do I change the wallpaper, the stone or the colour of the walls?
column3: Click a wall. In “Colour and texture”, each side has its covering (render, cut stone, brick, half-timbering, panelling, wallpaper, toile de Jouy, tiles, limewash…) and its colour. “Pattern size” enlarges the bricks or the paper. “Same for: the room / the whole floor / the whole house” copies the choice. In a room, “🧱 Room walls” changes all its walls at once. Floor tab: plain or beamed ceiling.

column2: How do I keep or share my house settings?
column3: 🧲 Snap → “💾 Saved settings”: “＋ Save the current settings” (snapping, grid, wall thickness, eye height, light), then ⋯ → “⤓ Export” for a .json file and “⤒ Import” on another computer.

column2: How do I export my house?
column3: “⤓ Export”: the floor plan as PNG, JPG, PDF or SVG, printing, an image of the 3D view, or the house file (.json) to import again with ⤒ Import. “Also keep a copy in the media” keeps the image in your media.

column2: Does colour blindness correction also apply in the editors?
column3: Yes: Settings → Accessibility → “Colours easy to tell apart” corrects the whole screen, including the 3D house, drawing, layout, retouching, tables, the map and full-screen windows. Your own colours are not replaced: the correction makes them distinguishable.

column2: How do I make the app easier to read or use (colour blindness, large text, voice)?
column3: Settings → Accessibility. Colours: choose your type of colour blindness (protanopia, deuteranopia…) — the app corrects its colours, with colours that are easy to tell apart and shapes (✓ ⚠ ⛔, hatching) in addition; “See as…” shows the screen as a colour-blind person sees it, to check an announcement or a chart. Text: size, line spacing, spacing, very legible font or one for dyslexia, underlined links. Also: high contrast, visible keyboard outline, big buttons, big pointer, fewer animations, messages shown for longer, and reading aloud (select a text then 🔊, or “Read the record”; Esc stops). “↺ Reset to default” puts everything back as at the start (“↶ Undo” in the message to go back).

column2: How do I choose a person, a place or something else in a tool?
column3: Everywhere, the same box: type 2 letters (surname, first name, town…). For each person the list shows their initials or photo (blue male, pink female, orange 🐾 animal), their dates and places, and their Sosa number; for a place, first those in your genealogy (blue marker, number of events), then the communes of France and the cities of the world (white marker) — the list scrolls without limit, and you can narrow it down by typing the department, its number or the country (“saint-martin 32”, “springfield usa”). ↑ ↓ to choose, Enter to confirm, Esc to close; “＋ Create the record” if it does not exist. Once chosen, the person becomes a badge with “↗ Record” and × to change. You can also type “sosa 12” or “#45” (record number).

column2: How do I choose an image from my media in a tool?
column3: Everywhere (announcements, layout, retouching, slideshow, presentation, montage, boards, museum, seals, dashboard…), the same window opens: your media as thumbnails. Type a title, a reference, a name, a place or a year; the buttons at the top filter (Photos, Documents, Sounds, Videos, the tool’s person, 🕘 Recent, ⭐ Portraits) and show how many there are. Click an image to see it large on the right (with its size and the format it prints well in), double-click or press Enter to take it. When you can take several, tick them (click or Space) then “Use these images”. An image from the computer? Drag it into the window, paste it (⌘V) or “📁 Import…”: it goes into your media and is ticked. The thumbnail size (large, small, list) is remembered.

column2: Vector drawing: how do I cut out a group or a layer with a shape (mask)?
column3: Place the cutting shape (circle, oval, heart, outline of a commune, escutcheon…) at the very top of the group or layer, then, in the Layers panel, click ✂️ on the line of the group or layer: you only see what is inside the shape (portrait in a medallion, map cut to the outline of a commune, motif in a coat of arms). Nothing is erased: a 2nd click on ✂️ removes the mask and the shape goes back to the very top. The coloured ✂️ shows what is masked. For a few objects without a group: select them with the shape on top, then Object → “Clipping mask” (⌘7).

column2: Announcements: more formats, and adding, removing or hiding fields?
column3: In the announcement window, “Format” offers cards (10 × 15 to 16 × 22 cm), squares (12 to 21 cm), long formats (DL, menu, bookmark, banner), posters (A4 to A1, 40 × 60, 50 × 70, 60 × 80 cm), screen formats (social networks, story, email, 16:9) and “Custom” where you type the width and height in cm. Each field has a checkbox (unticked: the field stays in the window but is not printed), ↑ ↓ to arrange it and 🗑 to remove it. “＋ Add a field” creates a new one, with its size (small, normal, large, calligraphic title), italic and bold. “Put back a removed field” and “↺ Reset to default” go back to the template. The chosen fields and format are remembered for next time.

column2: How do I organise a family reunion?
column3: Lists → Research and organisation → “🎉 Family reunions” → “＋ New family reunion” (or ⋯ on the ancestor’s record → “🎉 Organise a family reunion…”, or Lists → Editing tools). Choose the ancestor, or the couple: the app finds all their living descendants (and their spouses, if you tick it), arranged by branch, with their relationship to the ancestor (“grandson of…”) and to a reference person, usually you (“second cousin of…”). A person with no death recorded, born less than 100 years ago, is marked “Living?”: check. Confidential records are never shown.

column2: Where do I put the addresses and replies of the family reunion guests?
column3: “👥 Guests” tab: the ✓ box says who is invited; the address, email and phone come from the directory of the living or from the last address on the record. You change them here without touching the record (unless you tick “also in the directory of the living”). The reply (yes, no, maybe), the number of people and the diet are noted on each line. “⤒ Import a list…” reads a table (CSV, Excel .xlsx, LibreOffice .ods) with a line of headings (First name, Surname, Email, Reply…); “↶ Undo” undoes it.

column2: How do I send the invitations for the family reunion?
column3: “✉️ Invitations” tab: write the text once ({foyer}, {date}, {lieu}… are replaced by themselves); one invitation per household (the descendant, their spouse and their minor children). “🖨 Print the invitations…” (one page per household, the address for a window envelope, “⤓ PDF”), “📝 In the word processor”, “📰 Announcement (drawing)”, “📁 Copy in the media”. “✉️ Email ready” opens your email program with the text: nothing is sent by the app.

column2: How do I make the badges, the big tree and the seating plan for the family reunion?
column3: “🏷 Badges”: an A4 sheet (6, 8 or 10 badges), the first name in large print, the branch in colour, the relationship, the small photo and a QR code if you like. “🌳 Big tree”: all the descendants in large format (A2, A1…), one colour per branch, boxes to stick the photos of the day; it opens in the drawing tool to export it as PDF for the printer (bleed, crop marks). “📅 D-day”: the attendance list, the seating plan by branch (a household is never separated, ↶ Undo) and the photo album. “📊 Figures”: guests and replies by branch, and the colour of each branch.

column2: Do the family reunion addresses leave the app?
column3: No: they stay in the family reunion project. No export (GEDCOM, website, simple mode, view-only mode) reads them. The only file that takes them out is “⤓ Export ▾ → Guest table (CSV)”, and the addresses, emails and phone numbers are only in it if you tick the box.

column2: How do I make an announcement, an invitation or a poster for a family reunion?
column3: Lists → Editing tools → “📰 Announcements and posters” (or Charts). Choose the kind (birth, baptism, marriage, death, family reunion, golden wedding, old newspaper article, invitation), a style (Belle Époque, Art Nouveau, Art Deco, 1950s, classic, modern, mourning) and a format; choose a person from the tree: names, dates, places, ages and family fill in by themselves. The result opens in the vector tool: each text, ornament and the photo can be edited, then you print (or PDF) and export (PNG, JPG, SVG).

column2: How do I make a slideshow or the story in pictures of an ancestor?
column3: Lists → Editing tools → “🎞️ Presentation and slideshow”. “✨ A person’s story” builds the slideshow of a life by itself: a title, their photos, a map where the route of the places of their life is drawn, their biography. You then add photos (with a slow camera movement), titles, route maps (a migration: places to add, or those of a person’s life), your voice on each slide (🎙), music that lowers when the voice speaks; you play it full screen and export it as a video (Media or download).

column2: How do I make a presentation as with Keynote or PowerPoint?
column3: Lists → Editing tools → “🎞️ Presentation and slideshow” → “＋ New” → “🎤 Presentation (Keynote style)”, then choose a theme and a format (16:9, 4:3, square, vertical, A4, custom). On the left the slides (drag them to arrange them; ⧉ duplicate, 👁 skip during playback, § start a section that folds up); “＋ Slide ▾” offers the layouts: title, title and text, title and photo, full-page photo, photo and text, two columns, quote, section, key figure, a person. At the top: insert a text, a shape (rectangle, ellipse, star, arrow, bubble, line…), an image, a table, a chart, the record, the portrait, the small tree or the timeline of the life of a person from the database, a video or a sound. An object can be moved, enlarged (⇧: proportions, ⌥: from the centre), rotated (top handle) and aligned with the others thanks to the guides; ⌥ while dragging copies it. On the right, the inspector: Format (font, size, bold, lists, colours, border, shadow, cropping and masking of photos…), Animate, Slide (colour, gradient or image background, notes), Objects (front, back, hide, lock) and Document (theme, fonts, format, music). ⌘Z undoes, ⌘C ⌘V copy (also from one presentation to another), ⌘G groups, ⌘L locks.
